question: Should `/v1/chat/completions` ever expose internal OpenClaw agent tool calls, and if so through what opt-in, redacted, scoped contract?
rationale: Current code and shipped docs intentionally expose caller-supplied client tools only; expanding this boundary is both a product API decision and a sensitive telemetry/security decision.

options.title: Keep client-tool boundary
options.body: Continue returning OpenAI-compatible `tool_calls` only for caller-supplied HTTP tools and direct internal-tool debugging to existing Gateway/session diagnostic surfaces.

options.title: Design redacted diagnostic mode
options.body: Add a separate opt-in diagnostic/API surface for internal tool telemetry with explicit scopes, redaction, docs, and compatibility tests.

options.title: Expose internals in Chat Completions
options.body: Broaden the Chat Completions response shape to include internal tool calls, accepting the compatibility and sensitive-context exposure risk.

recommendation.title: Keep client-tool boundary
recommendation.body: Continue returning OpenAI-compatible `tool_calls` only for caller-supplied HTTP tools and direct internal-tool debugging to existing Gateway/session diagnostic surfaces.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice crosses Gateway API compatibility and security-sensitive product policy, and steipete has adjacent tool-contract history plus repository routing context.
